subject: Hospitality
title: Attribute-Based Selling
description: A micro-lesson that makes Attribute-Based Selling usable.

hook.text: Instead of booking 'a standard room,' what if you picked floor, view, bed type, and quietness level—each priced separately?

buildup.text: Attribute-based selling (ABS) unbundles the room into features. Pay $20 extra for a high floor, $30 for a city view.

discovery.text: Airlines already do this—seat selection, legroom, baggage are all priced separately. Hotels are moving toward the same model.

twist.text: ABS generates more revenue per room by letting guests customize. But it also risks frustrating guests who feel nickel-and-dimed.

climax.text: The balance is offering choice without overwhelming. Too many options paralyze guests; too few miss revenue opportunities.

punchline.text: Pick your view, pick your floor, pick your price. Rooms become configurable.

quiz.question: What is attribute-based selling in hotels?
options: Unbundling room features—view, floor, bed type—and pricing each separately
